title: About
text:
Economist · Quantitative Analyst · Reproducible-Research Advocate

I help economists and analysts turn data and code into research they can trust, reproduce, and publish.
I am a PhD economist with more than 25 years of experience in research and quantitative analysis. I spent nearly fifteen years as a Senior Economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and seven as a Senior Policy Economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland. Today I validate statistical, machine-learning, and GenAI models at KeyBank. I studied at the University of Rochester and ITAM, and my research spans a wide variety of fields in economics.






Research

70+ articles on regional and urban economics, public finance, banking, labor and migration, and forecasting. Browse the research or explore the map of how the papers relate.



Reproducible research

A long-time user and advocate of version control, Linux, and literate programming. I teach economists and analysts Git, Make, Quarto, and Git-friendly notebooks so their work can be rerun, reviewed, and published with confidence.



Models & AI

I validate credit, fraud, AML, and marketing models, collaborate on reviews of LLM proofs of concept, and build Python/Rust automation and network visualization tools for model risk management.


More detail is in my résumé and CV.
